Hi Alice, Ben, Marissa —

Thanks for the context. I put together the attached "retention_holdchain_playbook_v1.pdf" which covers the end-to-end delete pipeline at a tenant scope. High-level notes here:

- What is deleted: application-level inference logs (raw request/response payloads) and derived token-level indices are removed from the active serving cluster and metadata store within the configured retention window. For customers with a retention exception, we can extend logical retention windows per-tenant.
- Backups and snapshots: nightly snapshots are retained for disaster recovery for a configurable period. By default DR snapshots are immutable for 30 days; we can shorten this window for customers under SLA but we cannot retroactively remove snapshots without a coordinated procedure (we perform targeted snapshot scrubbing upon approved legal removal requests).
- KV cache and serving caches: we flush and revoke cache tokens upon delete; however, ephemeral in-memory caches may persist for a short time until rotation. Our proof-of-delete runbook includes steps to verify eviction and re-seed checks.
- Indices and search: we run a reindex operation that excises tenant-scoped shards; we then surface a proof artifact that includes deletion timestamps and shard IDs.
- Key rotation & pseudonymization: for customers needing stronger non-recoverability we offer a key-rotation + pseudonymization workflow that makes historical entries irrecoverable without an escrow key.

Attachments included:
- retention_holdchain_playbook_v1.pdf — overview + playbook steps
- Neurolytics_SIG_questions_filled.pdf — the SIG pages we filled in referencing our controls
- sample_proof_of_delete_guidelines.txt (included in the PDF bundle)

A couple of caveats to surface for your legal team:
1) If Neurolytics requires that a copy be retained under your custody (escrow) while Redwood deletes tenant data elsewhere, we can support a managed escrow flow but it requires a standing amendment to the contract (scope, access controls, custody transfer procedures).
2) Deleting data from third-party backups (cloud snapshots held by hyperscalers) is handled via our provider deletion request; timelines depend on provider retention windows and may require coordination.

If helpful I can join the call to walk the team through the playbook and provide example artifacts (shard IDs, timestamps).

—Marcus

Appreciate the questions — we can cover each on the call. Quick answers so you can triage with counsel:
- Snapshot scrubbing timeline: targeted snapshot scrubs typically complete within 3–7 business days after authorization for standard cloud providers; we’ll provide an expected date range when we see the specific snapshot metadata.
- Escrow KMS options: we support customer-managed CMKs (AWS KMS) for escrow scenarios; customer holds the key and we never have plaintext access. We also offer Redwood-managed escrow (HSM) for customers that want us to operate the custody with strict access audits — that requires an amendment.
- Proof artifacts: attaching the custody_chain.xlsx (sanitized sample) and the SIG PDF pages we filled out. On the call Marcus will show an example proof-of-delete package (CSV with shard/trace IDs and removal timestamps).
